meta.title: Standards & Architecture - CARE Platform
meta.description: CARE is designed around FHIR R5, SNOMED CT, LOINC, UCUM, ICD-10, ABDM alignment, open APIs, terminology services, and self-hostable deployment models.

hero.title: Standards-first by design, not integration as an afterthought.
hero.body: CARE is designed as a standards-first core: configurable forms, FHIR-aligned resources, terminology bindings, plugins, open APIs, sovereign hosting, and AI-ready structured data.

standards.title: CARE speaks the language of modern health systems.

items.fhir: FHIR-aligned resources and APIs for modern health data exchange and workflow modeling.
items.snomed: Clinical terminology direction for structured observations, findings, procedures, and concepts.
items.loinc: Laboratory and observation coding for diagnostic and measurement workflows.
items.ucum: Standard units for measurements, vitals, labs, and quantitative observations.
items.icd10: Classification support for diagnosis grouping, reporting, and program analytics.
items.abdm: India digital health alignment through CARE Apps and integration patterns.

architecture.title: Modular workflows on a shared clinical data foundation.
architecture.body: CARE avoids treating interoperability as a later integration project. The platform uses structured resources, configurable forms, terminology, and APIs so deployments can adapt locally while preserving data reuse.

forms.title: Configurable forms
forms.description: Questionnaires and EMR forms map operational workflows to structured clinical data.

terminology.title: Terminology bindings
terminology.description: Bring-your-own terminology and shared terminology services can align local workflows with standards.

apis.title: Open APIs
apis.description: API-first architecture lets hospitals, governments, and partners integrate without closed vendor gates.

plugins.title: Plugin extensibility
plugins.description: Apps and integrations extend CARE for national rails, TeleICU, AI documentation, labs, pharmacy, billing, and analytics.

deployment.title: Health systems should be able to own their infrastructure and data.
deployment.body: CARE is self-hostable and cloud-agnostic. Governments and institutions can run it in their own infrastructure, integrate with national systems, and maintain local control over data and operations.

ai.title: AI works best when the underlying health record is structured, traceable, and interoperable.
ai.body: OHC frames AI as assistive and human-in-the-loop. CARE can support voice-native forms, documentation drafts, summarization, and document understanding because workflows are connected to structured data and audit trails.
